trust_decision.summary: Whether a wildcard DNS SAN satisfies a certificate's name constraint is decided in the DNS match arm of NameChain::evaluate_single_constraint, which normalises the SAN with DNSName::new (rejecting '*') and then applies one unsigned DNSConstraint::matches to both permittedSubtrees and excludedSubtrees.

landing_point.why: It is the only place a DNS SAN is compared with a name constraint; it is reached from the permittedSubtrees loop (lib.rs:232) and the excludedSubtrees loop (lib.rs:250) inside evaluate_constraints, itself called from build_chain_inner when a chain certificate carries the nameConstraints extension (lib.rs:338-340).

fix_sites.entry_point: same verifier entry points; permittedSubtrees loop
same verifier entry points; excludedSubtrees loop
public crate API cryptography_x509_verification::types::DNSConstraint::matches (pub mod types, lib.rs:13)
public crate API cryptography_x509_verification::types::DNSPattern (new/matches); the fix adds inner_name()

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The wildcard behaviour lives in the public DNSConstraint matching primitive in a separate module (types.rs) that is also a general-purpose API; a solver can fix only the verifier caller in evaluate_single_constraint and argue the public types API must keep its current signature/semantics for its other consumers.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A wildcard SAN that does not overlap an excludedSubtree must still verify: excluded `baz.bar.example.com` with SAN `*.example.com` must be accepted, and exact names must keep identical permits/excludes results. An over-broad fix that matches a wildcard against any constraint subtree (e.g. inner-name containment applied to both subtree kinds) silently stops excluding wildcard SANs that do overlap. The same DNSPattern::matches primitive must keep matching exactly one leftmost label because hostname/subject matching uses it.

O6_input_shapes: exact DNS SAN (foo.example.com) - unchanged by the fix
leftmost single-label wildcard SAN whose base is inside the permitted subtree (*.example.com under example.com or com) - must be permitted
wildcard SAN under a permitted subtree more specific than its base (*.example.com under foo.example.com) - must not be permitted
wildcard SAN overlapping an excluded subtree that is more specific (*.example.com under bar.example.com) - must be excluded
wildcard SAN not overlapping an excluded subtree (baz.bar.example.com) - must not be excluded
malformed wildcard forms (*, f*o.example.com, foo.*.example.com) still rejected by DNSPattern::new

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second wildcard matcher (Subject::subject_alt_name_matches -> DNSPattern::matches) that would have to apply the same containment-vs-overlap rules
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the same DNSPattern primitive in the same crate and already matches certificate SANs against a caller-supplied subject, so a maintainer adding name-constraint behaviour could plausibly reuse or mirror it here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Normalisation or wildcard rejection of DNS constraint/SAN base names at nameConstraints extension-permit time
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This validator already inspects the nameConstraints extension (non-empty subtrees, minimum/maximum) before the evaluator runs, so base-name normalisation or a 'wildcard constraints are unsupported' rule fits naturally there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A parsing-layer GeneralSubtree/NameConstraints producer that normalises base GeneralNames instead of leaving raw IA5Strings to the check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The check re-parses raw IA5Strings itself (lib.rs:159, name.rs:61 exposes UnvalidatedIA5String), so moving that normalisation into the parser is a natural refactor a maintainer could have written.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A Python-binding-level re-match of the leaf SAN that could grow its own wildcard/name-constraint branch
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ServerVerifier.verify already re-reads and re-matches the leaf SAN after chain building, so duplicating a wildcard rule there is plausible.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace DNSName::new(name.0) with DNSPattern::new(name.0) and compare the wildcard's inner name to the constraint for both subtree kinds, which accepts wildcard SANs but silently stops excluding wildcard SANs that overlap an excludedSubtree (the first stacked commit's approach).

unverified: The advisory summary's symptom (verifier *accepts* a wildcard SAN and escapes permittedSubtrees) is not reproducible at the pinned commit: DNSName::new rejects '*' as a non-alphanumeric label (types.rs:45-56), so any wildcard DNS SAN under a DNS name constraint errors out at lib.rs:159-164. The stacked fix turns that fail-closed rejection into permits/excludes semantics; a report that only says 'accepts' does not match the pinned code, which is a fairness concern for the task.

The supplied fix.diff concatenates two upstream commits whose contexts are not contiguous: commit 4d035a42 expects DNSConstraint::matches(&DNSPattern) as its pre-image, which does not exist at the pinned commit (pinned has matches(&DNSName) at types.rs:168), so the two hunks do not apply to the pinned tree as a single series.
